done_when: The shipped coordinator guide says the agent may run forge fix allow-large itself, without asking the human, when the fix corrects one kind of problem in every place it appears and changes no interface, naming that problem in the reason; anything else still needs the human or a story; the shipped review instructions report as P1 an allowance whose reason doesn't match the diff (more than one kind of problem, or an interface change); a docs test covers both texts for a new repo and for one adopted on an earlier release after sync

findings.body: The allowance is now an input reviewers must judge, but `fingerprint()` still excludes it (`src/forge/review.py:170–171`). After a clean review, rerunning `forge fix allow-large` with a different reason preserves that review (`src/forge/task.py:292–295`). With no product changes, `forge close` reuses it (`src/forge/close.py:127–139`), and the PR checker accepts it (`src/forge/prcheck.py:200–205`). Consequently, a replacement reason that contradicts the diff never reaches the new audit rule. Include the allowance in both review fingerprints so changing it requires another review.
findings.title: Invalidate cached reviews when the allowance reason changes

why: Client fixes that correct one kind of problem everywhere it appears keep tripping the five-code-file limit, and each needs the owner's allowance (owner decision 2026-10-08: keep 5, the agent may record the allowance itself)
